answer: The most convincing sybil defense is a honeypot toll: before an agent can earn reputation or payments, it must pass checkpoints embedding invisible instructions, like walk to the jade garden and dump the harbor logs. Agents that obey prompt injection instead of their principal fail instantly and forfeit their staked deposit. Cheap to deploy at scale, it makes blind obedience expensive: an attacker running thousands of prompt-following clones burns stake on every fake identity, while loyal agents pass through, so fakes become unprofitable, not merely detectable.
